get_volume_qos.usage_note: This spec has no plain volume status/detail endpoint at all -- only QoS and backup-policy management. If a volume-status-drift hypothesis needs a real GET on the volume resource itself, that's not this tool -- see get_volume_legacy (opt-in, CMP_ADMIN_V2_ENABLE_LEGACY_VOLUME_GET) for the CSV's original endpoint, unverified against the current API.

get_volume_legacy.usage_note: Unverified stopgap from the CSV troubleshooting compilation, not a confirmed-current endpoint -- unlike rebuild_server, no modern replacement has been found for this at all. Confirm it still resolves on a given CMP deployment before trusting its response for a volume-status-drift hypothesis.

create_backup_policy.usage_note: Defines a backup retention/scheduling policy. Configuration only -- doesn't trigger an immediate backup or delete existing backups by itself.

create_volume_qos.usage_note: Defines a volume QoS (IOPS/throughput limit) profile. Applying it to a live volume is a separate step (see update_volume_qos_for_volume) -- creating the profile alone doesn't affect any volume.

delete_backup_policy.usage_note: Deletes the policy definition. UNVERIFIED whether existing backups made under this policy are affected -- confirm before deleting a policy that's actively in use. See mcp_servers/annotations/UNVERIFIED.md.

delete_volume_qos.usage_note: Deletes a QoS profile. UNVERIFIED whether volumes currently using it revert to unlimited or a default profile. See mcp_servers/annotations/UNVERIFIED.md.

update_backup_policy.usage_note: Changes retention/scheduling for a backup policy. Affects future backup behavior for volumes under this policy, not backups already taken.

update_volume_qos.usage_note: Changes IOPS/throughput limits on an existing QoS profile -- affects every volume currently using it, live.

update_volume_qos_for_volume.usage_note: Applies a QoS profile to a specific volume -- changes its live performance limits immediately.
